nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused transformer block (Swin-W-MSA + MLP). Mix of GEMM-like ops (Linear), reductions (LayerNorm, softmax), and elementwise (GELU, residual). N=16 (window), C=32 (channels), hidden=128. nWindows=57600, B=1. 2) Canonical math: y1=x+Proj(Attn(LN1(x))); y2=y1+FC2(GELU(FC1(LN2(y1)))). Attention: per-window 16x16 softmax((q@kT)/sqrt(C)+rpe)@v. 3) Layout: input (1,720,1280,32) row-major last-dim=C. Window partition reshapes 4x4 blocks of HxW into windows. With Wh=Ww=4 and contiguous C=32, each window's 16 tokens are NOT contiguous (stride along W). We can iterate windows by (b,nh,nw) and gather 16 tokens of 32 floats each = 16*32*2=1024B per window per pass. 4) Regimes: a) memory-bound (whole block end-to-end) -> fuse aggressively; b) small-matmul regime per window -> coalesce many windows per program; c) softmax reduction over N=16 -> trivial in registers. 5) Knobs: tile = group of windows per program; fuse LN+QKV; fuse attention+proj+residual; fuse LN2+FC1+GELU+FC2+residual; numerics: fp32 accum for LN/softmax. 6) Skeleton: Kernel A: LN1+QKV+Attention+Proj+residual writing y1 with window-reverse. Kernel B: LN2+FC1+GELU+FC2+residual to produce y. Possibly split QKV from attention if register pressure too high. 7) Families: F1 fully fused two-kernel design (per-window programs); F2 sub-fused (LN+QKV separate; attention+proj fused; LN2+MLP fused); F3 reuse torch matmul for linears, custom kernel only for attention+softmax+RPE.

action.description: Implement one Triton kernel that, per program, processes a tile of M windows. For each window: load 16x32 tokens, compute LN1 (fp32 reduction), compute QKV via small fused matmul (32->96), split into q,k,v (16x32 each), compute attn = softmax(q@k^T * scale + rpe), compute o=attn@v, apply proj (32->32) + bias, add residual, write back in window-reverse layout. Use fp32 accumulation for LN and softmax; tl.dot for matmuls or manual broadcast multiplies given small dims.
action.rationale: Fusing all attention-side ops avoids 4-5 round-trips through global memory of the 56MB activation tensor.

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin block at fp16 on a (1,720,1280,32) input with single-head W-MSA over 4x4 windows (N=16, C=32) followed by an MLP with hidden=128. The block is composed of two LayerNorms, three Linears (QKV 32->96, Proj 32->32, FC1 32->128, FC2 128->32), an attention with relative position bias, softmax, GELU, and two residual adds. Activation tensor is ~56MB so the workload is heavily memory-bandwidth bound; the natural plan is to write two fused Triton kernels — one for LN1+QKV+Attention+Proj+Residual (per-window) and one for LN2+FC1+GELU+FC2+Residual (per-row) — using fp32 accumulation for LN/softmax. Small inner dims (16/32/128) and small weight matrices favor weight caching in registers/SLM and grouping multiple windows/rows per program. Target: beat torch.compile by reducing global memory round-trips and fusing reshape/permute layout ops.
open_questions: Does Triton's XPU backend support tl.dot efficiently at these small K=32 dims, or is manual broadcast-multiply-reduce faster?
What is the exact GELU formulation used by nn.GELU here (exact erf vs tanh approx) at fp16 — required for tolerance?
How costly are strided loads when gathering 4x4 windows from the (H,W,C) tensor on Arc Pro B70's memory hierarchy?
Are LayerNorm weight/bias and Linear bias all fp16 in this configuration, and is fp32 accumulation needed to match reference numerics?
What's the best windows-per-program (M tile) to balance occupancy vs register pressure on Xe2 subgroup size 16?
Can we keep FC1/FC2 weights (32x128 + 128x32 fp16, ~16KB) resident in registers across an entire program tile?
Does torch.compile already fuse the MLP path effectively on XPU, so the speedup must come primarily from attention fusion?
Is rpe_bias broadcast across all windows correctly and small enough (1x1x16x16) to load once per program?
